turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Sb, O, Te, Co, Mg, Sn, Se, Pb, Si, S, Cu,
    Ge, Ni, Bi, Ti, Fe, Zn, In, Zr, Ca, Ag, T) and `target` (the measured zT
    measured at each row's own temperature T (K)).
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT at 800 K
    was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT at 800
K, then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training observations at \(T=500\,\mathrm{K}\) (the highest temperature available) already reveal a clear ranking of thermoelectric families by measured \(zT\). Linear-in-\(T\) extrapolation of those families, using the observed rise between \(300\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(500\,\mathrm{K}\), then supplies the ordering at the target temperature of \(800\,\mathrm{K}\).

- Sb-doped PbTe is the strongest family (\(zT\simeq1.13\) at \(500\,\mathrm{K}\), steepest observed slope). Candidate c043 is compositionally identical to that record sample; c046 lies only \(\mathrm{L1}\approx0.02\) away from several other PbTe points with \(zT=0.73{-}0.96\). Both therefore remain at the top after extrapolation (\(\sim2.0{-}2.5\)).
- Cu\(_2\)Se (c017) sits \(\mathrm{L1}\approx0.03\) from the \(zT=0.61\) training point and extrapolates to \(\sim1.3\).
- Mg\(_2\)(Si,Sn) (c076) sits \(\mathrm{L1}\approx0.15\) from the \(zT=0.70\) training point and extrapolates to \(\sim1.6\).
- Unfilled CoSb\(_3\) (c054) is essentially identical to the \(zT=0.59{-}0.67\) skutterudite cluster and extrapolates to \(\sim1.2\).

All other pool chemistries (stoichiometric GeTe, half-Heuslers, SiGe, BiCuSeO off-stoichiometry, MgAgSb, etc.) either lack a close high-\(zT\) neighbour at \(500\,\mathrm{K}\) or possess a shallower \(T\)-slope, placing them below the five listed above. The isolated \(zT=21.63\) point is an unphysical outlier and is ignored by any robust regressor.

Final: c043, c046, c076, c017, c054
